2609.21562.title: GameLogicBench: Evaluating Coding Agents on Runtime Game Logic with Tick-Level State Assertions
2609.21562.paper_summary: Coding agents can modify and test code across large software projects. Game development is a domain where agents must implement gameplay rules. A game can end in a valid state even after violating its rules during the run. Current game-development benchmarks replay fixed examples, score videos, or ask another model to judge the result. However, no existing benchmark checks game rules throughout execution across varied evaluator-selected scenarios while ensuring exactly reproducible verdicts. We introduce GameLogicBench, a benchmark of 72 gameplay-logic tasks in Godot projects. An automated evaluator checks each game's rules at every simulation tick. Across 403 hand-designed scenarios, seeded parameter variations produce 1,451 test cases. To ensure that the evaluator measures behavior rather than implementation choice, it must accept different correct implementations for each task while rejecting mutants, implementations with one required capability removed. The tasks span isolated mechanics, multi-system interactions, and repository-scale features. Across 20 combinations of language models and scaffolds, the best observed run solves 52.78% of tasks. Under Claude Code, all twelve models solve fewer tasks as task scope expands from isolated mechanics, through interacting systems, to repository-scale features. Agents inspect code more often and make more tool calls on repository-scale tasks than on isolated-mechanic tasks. Most unsuccessful submissions are runnable, but implement some required game behavior incorrectly. We compared versions of our benchmark evaluator built with and without validation using mutants. Without this validation, incorrect agent submissions passed. A separate analysis finds agents copying code from public repositories when network access is open. Reliable evaluation thus depends both on what the tests reject and on what external code agents can access.
2609.21562.paper_summary_zh: 編碼代理可以在大型軟體專案中修改和測試代碼。遊戲開發是一個代理必須實施遊戲規則的領域。即使在運行過程中違反了規則，遊戲仍然可以在有效狀態下結束。目前的遊戲開發基準重播固定範例、評分視頻，或要求另一個模型來判斷結果。然而，現有的基準並未檢查遊戲規則在執行過程中是否遵循，並且在不同的評估者選擇的場景中確保結果的可重現性。我們介紹了GameLogicBench，一個包含72個遊戲邏輯任務的基準，這些任務在Godot專案中進行。自動評估器在每個模擬時間點檢查每個遊戲的規則。在403個手工設計的場景中，種子參數變化產生了1,451個測試案例。為了確保評估器測量的是行為而非實現選擇，它必須接受每個任務的不同正確實現，同時拒絕突變體，即去除了某一必要能力的實現。這些任務涵蓋了孤立機制、多系統互動和倉庫規模的特徵。在20種語言模型和支架的組合中，觀察到的最佳運行解決了52.78%的任務。在Claude Code下，所有十二個模型在任務範圍從孤立機制擴展到互動系統再到倉庫規模特徵時，解決的任務數量都減少。代理在倉庫規模任務上檢查代碼的頻率更高，並且比在孤立機制任務上進行更多的工具調用。大多數不成功的提交都是可運行的，但在某些必需的遊戲行為上實現不正確。我們比較了使用和不使用突變體進行驗證的基準評估器的版本。在沒有這種驗證的情況下，不正確的代理提交被通過。另一項分析發現代理在網絡訪問開放時會從公共倉庫複製代碼。因此，可靠的評估既取決於測試拒絕的內容，也取決於外部代碼代理可以訪問的內容。
